EDEKA24 Lebensmittel tree: Backen & Desserts (Margarine, Backzutaten, Mehl-Backpulver-Hefe, Nuesse, Zucker); Fruehstueck (Honig, Konfituere, Nuss- und Schokocreme); Wuerzmittel & Bruehen (Oele, Bruehen, Essig, Feinwuerzmittel, Gewuerze-Kraeuter, Salz, Wuerzmischungen); Sossen (Ketchup-Mayonnaise, Senf-Meerrettich, Tomatensosse-Pesto, Wuerzsaucen, Grillsaucen, Salatdressing); Beilagen (Reis, Nudeln, Samen-Saaten, Huelsenfruechte, Knoedel-Kartoffelprodukte); Konserven; products listed by shape (Spaghetti, Fusilli, Penne Rigate, Tagliatelle) with makers Barilla De Cecco Delverde

Japanese Standard Tables of Food Composition 2010 table of contents: 18 food groups incl. 1 Cereals, 3 Sugars and sweeteners, 4 Pulses, 5 Nuts and seeds, 14 Fats and oils, 17 Seasonings and spices (subgroups seasonings, spices, other); groups are by source organism then processing; confectionery and beverages separate

EU olive oil: eight categories (extra-virgin, virgin, lampante, refined, olive oil composed of refined and virgin, pomace oil, crude pomace, refined pomace); only four may be sold at retail; graded by physico-chemical and organoleptic parameters; Reg 2022/2104

Manuka rating systems UMF (4-marker certification by UMF Honey Association), MGO (mg/kg), NPA, KFactor (Wedderspoon proprietary); UMF 5+/10+/15+/20+ maps to MGO 83/263/514/829; a spec ladder measured on the product
Serious Eats rice guide groups rice by subspecies (indica, japonica) because subspecies predicts more than grain shape; long grain is mostly indica, short mostly japonica, with exceptions

DeLallo pasta shape guide: categories Long (lunga), Short (corta), Tube, Stuffed (ripiena), Cooked in broth (pastina), Stretched, Dumpling-like (gnocchi), Special shape; each cut sold in semolina, whole wheat, organic, gluten-free variants; named cuts Acini di Pepe, Bucatini, Fusilli, Manicotti, Spaghetti; ~400 shapes

Rancho Gordo heirloom beans sold by named variety (Domingo Rojo etc.), separate collections for Grains and Seeds, Herbs and Spices, Pantry Goods, Chiles and Sauces, Corn; bean variety is the unit buyers pick

BigBasket Foodgrains Oil & Masala (9272 items): facets Oil Type (olive, mustard, groundnut, sesame, coconut, rice bran, pomace, extra virgin), Dal Type (toor, moong, urad, masoor, chana, rajma), Millets (ragi, jowar, bajra, foxtail, kodo), Age of the Rice, Grain Type (split/whole), Powdered Spices (biryani, garam, chilli, sambar masala), flours (atta, besan, sooji, ragi); rice listed by variety (Sona Masoori, Ponni, Basmati, Matta, Idli); typical Indian cut mixes staples, oils, ghee and spices in one tree

myAsianStore pantry: Soy Sauces and Condiments (light, dark, oyster, hoisin, chili oil, vinegars); Instant Noodles; Pantry Staples (beans, grains, hot pot bases, soup mixes, cooking sauces); collections Cereal/Grain Flour, Bean Paste, Preserved Vegetables, Peanuts, Sugar, Seasoning, Canned Goods, Salted Eggs; bilingual Chinese labels (調味, 醋, 榨菜); an Asian cut keeps sauces, pastes and seasonings together

Codex GSFA food categories: 02 Fats and oils; 04 Fruit and vegetables incl pulses, seaweeds, nuts and seeds (fresh, frozen, dried, in vinegar/oil/brine, canned, purees and spreads such as peanut butter, fermented); 06 Cereals incl breakfast cereals and soybean products (06.8: tofu, semi-dehydrated, fermented); 11 Sweeteners incl honey (refined/raw sugars, brown sugar, syrups, table-top); 12 Salts, spices, soups, sauces, salads, protein products (12.1 salt, 12.2 herbs and spices, 12.4 mustards, 12.6 sauces, 12.9 soybean products); 15 processed nuts as snacks. Splits by processing state not by crop

USDA SR/Foundation food categories relevant: Cereal Grains and Pasta; Fats and Oils; Legumes and Legume Products; Nut and Seed Products; Spices and Herbs; Sweets; Soups Sauces and Gravies; Baked Products; example kinds Pasta dry enriched spaghetti vs whole grain spaghetti

ISO 3632-1:2025 Spices, Saffron (Crocus sativus L.) Part 1 Specification, edition 3 2025-07, applies to filaments, cut filaments and powder; ISO/TC 34/SC 7 Spices, culinary herbs and condiments; saffron grade categories (I-III) are set in the standard text (not visible on page)

Carrefour epicerie salee children: Aperitifs et Chips; Huiles Vinaigres et Vinaigrettes (Huiles, Huiles d'olive, Vinaigres, Vinaigres balsamiques, Vinaigrettes); Pates; Sauces chaudes; Sauces froides; Conserves et Bocaux; Plats cuisines; Riz Purees et Feculents; Cornichons et condiments; Sel Epices et Bouillons; Soupes et Croutons; separate rayons Sucres Farines et Aide a la patisserie, Epicerie sucree, Fruits et Legumes secs, Saveurs asiatiques/italiennes (cuisine as a rayon); filter facets Labels qualite (AOP, IGP, Label Rouge, Bio), Regimes, Origine, Format

Consorzio of Aceto Balsamico Tradizionale di Modena DOP: two types Affinato (at least 12 years) and Extravecchio (at least 25 years); DOP is cooked must only, PGI adds wine vinegar; designation protected, a legal tier set by ageing

Consorzio of Aceto Balsamico di Modena PGI labelling guidelines (May 2025): Invecchiato at least 3 years, Riserva at least 5 years; adjectives restricted; a protected-name tier ladder (PGI plain, Invecchiato, Riserva) distinct from the DOP Tradizionale

Saffron has two parallel ladders: ISO 3632 laboratory Categories I, II, III (crocin, picrocrocin, safranal limits; safranal 20-50 for Cat I) and traditional market cuts Super Negin, Negin, Sargol, Pushal, Konj; ISO category is a measured spec, market cut is a trade grade

Burlap and Barrel single-origin spices: filters Spice Type (chilis and paprikas, cinnamon, onions and garlic, salt and pepper, blends, extracts), Format (whole, ground, blends), Cuisine, Uses, Flavor profile, Heat level; direct-trade sourcing by farm and origin (Herati saffron, Korean gochugaru); maker identity matters in this specialist niche

German flour Type numbers (405, 550, 1050) are ash content in mg per 100 g dry flour; separate type series for spelt (630, 812, 1050) and rye (815, 997, 1150); wholemeal has no type; French T55 and US all-purpose and Italian Tipo 00 as international equivalents; flour kind = grain x type x use

Soy Sauce Information Centre: JAS divides soy sauce into five types (koikuchi about 80 percent of output, usukuchi about 10 percent, tamari, saishikomi, shiro), each a distinct product with its own use; regional origin tied to type; separate dashi soy sauce and tsuyu are non-JAS derived condiments

Japan Soy Sauce Technology Center on JAS: grade ladder Tokkyu / Jokyu / Hyojun set by total nitrogen (g/100ml), colour number and extract per type (for koikuchi 1.50 / 1.35 / 1.20 or more); Tokusen and Cho-tokusen labels need 10 and 20 percent more nitrogen than Tokkyu; JAS mark optional; a measured spec ladder with its standard named

USDA AMS voluntary grade standards for nuts: separate standards per nut and per form (Almonds in shell, Shelled Almonds, Brazil nuts, Filberts, Pecans in shell / shelled, Pistachios, Walnuts, Peanuts by Virginia/Runner/Spanish type, Peanut Butter, Mixed nuts); the unit of grading is nut species x form (in shell vs shelled)

Sugar kinds: demerara, muscovado, turbinado, sucanat, jaggery, piloncillo; differences are crystal size, moisture and molasses intensity; raw sugars are usually refined to some extent; kind identified by processing and region name

Honey is chosen first by floral source (clover, wildflower, manuka, orange blossom, buckwheat, acacia, lavender, eucalyptus; 15+ types); monofloral vs polyfloral; manuka carries UMF/MGO rating as a spec; floral origin called the single most important factor

Clovegarden pulses reference groups legumes by genus or species (Phaseolus American beans; Vigna Asian/African beans; lentils; peas; chickpeas; fava; soybeans; peanuts) with dal (split, peeled) and gram (Indian names) as cross-cutting terms; region only noted within entries

Retail panel data (Circana) separates plant-based meat (analogues in burger, sausage, meatball formats) from tofu, tempeh and seitan, which are traditional foods not marketed as analogues; tofu EUR 95.1m 2025; plant-based meat volume 3.7 times tofu+tempeh+seitan; private label vs brand shares tracked

Japan Grain Inspection Association rice taste ranking 2025 crop: 144 production-area x cultivar entries tasted against a blended Koshihikari reference; five ranks Toku-A (43 entries), A (70), A-prime (30), B, B-prime; the ranked unit is area-plus-cultivar (a named form), rank changes yearly (a dated tier entry)

JGIA states the taste ranking covers main production-area cultivar brands only and not all rice; sellers showing Toku-A must say it is not an evaluation of the product itself (consumer-protection rule): a dated, area-level tier, not a product spec

Olive Oil Times World Ranking from NYIOOC competition results: Gold 1.00 point, Silver 0.75, bonus for recent wins; ranks brands (5+ awards) and producers (12.5+ points), with history by hemisphere, country, cultivar and organic; a consensus tier for extra virgin olive oil attached to makers, not kinds

Salt kinds chosen by crystal size and job: table/iodized, kosher (no density standard; Diamond Crystal vs Morton differ), fine and coarse sea salt, flake/Maldon, fleur de sel, kala namak and flavoured salts, pickling salt; all mostly sodium chloride; teaspoon weights differ so maker matters at kosher level

Japanese noodles grouped by base: wheat (udon incl Sanuki and Inaniwa, kishimen, somen, ramen, instant ramen), buckwheat (soba, about 30 percent buckwheat standard), starch (harusame mung bean and potato, kuzukiri); named regional types are non-maker forms

Canned tomatoes: San Marzano is a variety grown in Campania; DOP certified cans (Rega, La Valle, DeLallo) vs San Marzano style; US has no DOP rule so the name is not protected; certification is a paid designation shown on the can, not on every product from the area
